name: The Ritz-Carlton, San Francisco
positioning: Luxury hotel in a 1909 Neoclassical landmark building on Nob Hill, with a cable car stop outside and a private Club Level
best_for: Travelers who want a Nob Hill base with the cable car outside the door
Guests who want suites with bay and landmark views and Club Lounge access

facts.text: The hotel is in Nob Hill, set within a 1909 Neoclassical landmark building.
Signature Suites are on the Club Level on the top floors of the hotel.
Parallel 37 is the hotel restaurant and serves Californian cuisine crafted with local ingredients.
Bruma pairs city-inspired cocktails with modern California cuisine.
The Ritz Kids program includes a special registration experience for children and a scavenger hunt.
In the evenings the hotel offers complimentary car service for trips within a one-mile radius.
Families can stay in two-bedroom connecting suites with city views.
Rooms have pillow-top mattresses and 100% combed cotton linens.

highlights.text: The one-bedroom Ritz-Carlton Suite has views of Coit Tower, Alcatraz Island and the San Francisco Bay.
The one-bedroom Presidential Suite has a furnished terrace overlooking the city's Financial District.
A cable car stops right outside the hotel's doors.
The Club Lounge offers complimentary food and beverage presentations four times each day: breakfast, lunch, evening hors d'oeuvres and cocktails, and desserts.

considerations.text: Club access requires an upgraded booking, and Marriott Bonvoy Elite Status does not provide complimentary access to the Club.
On-site valet parking is available for a daily fee.
WhataHotel notes the historic building has traditional room layouts.
